facts.text: The base node subscribes to cmd_vel (geometry_msgs/Twist) and publishes base_odom (nav_msgs/Odometry)
The node sends the motor command as left,right,checksum, where the checksum is the sum of the character lengths of the two wheel-speed strings
The node reads a reply line and splits it on ',' into two wheel speeds in deg/sec
The body twist is converted to wheel speeds with VR = vx + wheelSep/2.0*wz and VL = vx - wheelSep/2.0*wz, then to deg/sec with 180.0/math.pi/wheelRad
The node opens the serial port with a 10 s read timeout
The node uses string.split(line, ',') to split the reply line (the Python 2 module-level split API)
The shipped launch file configures the base node for /dev/uno at 57600 baud
The launch file declares wheel_separation (0.15 m) and wheel_radius (0.0335 m) arguments
The firmware parses the third field as the checksum and compares it with the command length minus 2 minus the checksum length
The firmware declares min_ref=110 and max_ref=350
The firmware adjusts nonzero wheel references using max_ref, min_ref and a steering correction
When the left wheel-speed reference is exactly zero, the firmware sets the left PWM outputs to 0
When the right wheel-speed reference is exactly zero, the firmware sets the right PWM outputs to 0
The firmware reports the two wheel speeds as integers in deg/sec with a CRLF terminator
The firmware declares timer_period=20 ms, odom_pub_period=40 ms and their ratio as odom_pub_thres
The firmware's odom_pub compile-time flag is false
When odom_pub is false the firmware prints '0,0' instead of the measured wheel speeds
The firmware sets the serial read timeout to 50 ms
On a bad checksum the firmware returns without zeroing the wheel references; the assignments are commented out
When no serial input is available, the firmware loop only delays 50 ms
